scope: Isolated instrumented decoder comparison on original PLY-3; no production change
traceChanges: Logging only in project-file-codec.ts and project-decoding-worker.ts. The diagnostic harness adds local-file selection, artifact-read and decoder-event tracing.

comparisons.name: MCP in-place import
comparisons.result: Passed with matching reopened geometry. The first 266108040-byte decompressed chunk completed reading and hashing; the decoder returned all four numeric buffers.

comparisons.name: GUI open of an existing file without immediate export
comparisons.result: The decoder returned and the GUI accepted replacement. The first subsequent public-MCP geometry-digest request lost its connection near the 4 GiB boundary, so geometry was not verified.

comparisons.name: Export then delete artifact, GUI open existing file without artifact reads
comparisons.result: Passed: GUI replacement completed and the source, cutter and extracted-part core geometry digests matched. The source scene was reconstructed from the same original scan but object IDs differed, so comparison matched digests across returned objects.

comparisons.name: Export, read the entire artifact in 262144-byte MCP calls, delete, then GUI open existing file
comparisons.result: Failed: decoder started but returned 'Array buffer allocation failed' at the first chunk. The GUI reported one failed file. The original scene was not independently checked after the failure.

experimentalCandidates: An isolated FileReader-based artifact-read conversion reached the first chunk's hashing stage but timed out; peak job bytes 4519333888. Log SHA-256 5f89faeb489167c88b20940a9289ab64c79bdcbedcbd77897ef8ad836503d66c.

Combining that conversion with incremental chunk hashing also timed out before reporting completion of the first chunk; peak job bytes 4312932352. Log SHA-256 f6e7e23e7ff885ddc6d8f5ede062381483a47872af7a00b35352429e860bfbc6. Neither candidate was applied.
interpretation: The matched controls demonstrate that the full artifact-read workload can make the subsequent allocation fail under the guard, while export and direct GUI open can succeed without those reads. This is not proof of a particular retained buffer, garbage-collection cause or universal GUI failure.
limitations: These are instrumented, single-run controls; timings and memory pressure vary. The passing GUI run does not cover post-reopen history or native Split parity.
The artifact-read sequence discards returned payloads rather than independently verifying every downloaded byte; this is an allocation diagnostic, not artifact integrity acceptance.
Some recorded guard peaks exceed the nominal limit. Cleanup is confirmed; no failed run is presented as passing.
